page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. It features 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core using x86_64 architecture. The server includes 96.0 GB of DDR5 memory rated at 7 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include a 480 MB L3 cache along with specialized instruction set extensions such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), AVX-512, and AES cryptography acceleration. The instance operates with burstable CPU allocation, provides an 11 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and carries no attached local storage.

Performance benchmarks highlight strong compute capabilities in vector and matrix instruction workloads. The instance achieves top-tier performance in Geekbench image processing and small-model LLM text generation reaching 348.34 tokens per second. In general processing tests, it maintains top 25% performance across software compilation, ray tracing, static web serving at 82.41 GB per second throughput, and Redis SET operations at 86.83 million operations per second. High read memory bandwidth is supported by cached read speeds of 3838.93 GB per second and uncached read speeds of 193.31 GB per second. However, its burstable CPU allocation profile places sustained multi-core stress testing in the middle 50% percentile, representing a execution tradeoff under continuous peak CPU loads.

The flex instance model delivers qualitative cost efficiency for compute workloads with fluctuating demand profiles. By pairing high DDR5 memory throughput and AMX hardware acceleration with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the c8i-flex.12xlarge offers dense compute performance without requiring attached local disk overhead. This instance configuration is suitable for static web serving, software build compilation, matrix-accelerated LLM inference, and in-memory caching.
